Workspace

Links and the command line

Two ways into Clew from outside it. A clew:// link opens a note at a heading or a line — from a task manager, a calendar entry, a launcher, a web page — or makes today's diary entry. The clew command does the same from a terminal, and exports a note too. Both only open and create: neither runs a vault's code or changes what you trust. (Neither is in 0.12.0, and neither is on the iPad yet.)

clew:// links

A link to a heading

clew://open?vault=Research&note=Projects/Grant%20proposal#Aims%20and%20scope

vault names the vault: the name of its folder, matched ignoring case, for a vault this device already knows (one that is open or on the recent list), or its full path — /Users/… or ~/…. Two known vaults with the same name are ambiguous, and the link is refused with two vaults are called "Research" — name it by its path. Leave vault out and the link means the vault in front, or the last one you had open.

note is the note's path inside the vault, as the file explorer shows it; .md is assumed when there is no extension. After it, # and a heading lands on that heading, or &line=12 on that line. A link is a URL, so a space is written %20, as in the example. With no note at all, clew://open?vault=Research just brings that vault forward.

Today's diary entry, and a new note

clew://new?vault=Research&daily=1
clew://new?vault=Research&note=Inbox/Call%20with%20Sam

new with daily=1 opens today's diary entry, creating it if it is not there yet. With a note it creates that note, empty — never over a file: if Inbox/Call with Sam.md exists, the new one is Call with Sam 1.md. Either way a notice says so — Created Inbox/Call with Sam.md, from a clew link or command. — so a note never appears unexplained.

Whatever a link opens goes into a tab of its own, or the tab already showing that note, and never replaces the note you were working on.

What a link can and cannot do

A link may sit on a web page or in an email you did not write, so there are only two actions. open opens and navigates; new makes an empty note or today's entry. Nothing else happens:

  • Anything else is refused by name. clew://run?… shows A clew link was refused: clew://run is not something a link can do (open, new).
  • A link never runs code or changes trust. A vault opened by a link is exactly as trusted or restricted as it was before.
  • A vault this device has not seen is asked about first: Open the vault "Elsewhere"? A clew:// link asked to open …, which Clew has not opened on this device. Opening it shows its notes; it does not trust its code. Cancel is the default. If you open it, it opens restricted, as any vault does the first time.
  • A note path cannot leave the vault. A path with .. in it, or an absolute one, is refused, and a note that does not exist gets No note "…" in Research. rather than being made.

Where links work

An installed Clew registers itself as the handler for clew:// links, so clicking one anywhere on the system opens what the link names — starting Clew first if it is not running, in the window Clew starts with rather than a second one. A Clew run from its source code (npm run dev) does not register on macOS — it would register the bare Electron app instead — so there you give it the link on its command line: electron . 'clew://open?vault=…'.

The clew command

Help → Install the clew Command… puts a clew command where your terminal finds commands: /usr/local/bin if your account may write there, otherwise ~/.local/bin. It never asks for an administrator's password, and if the folder it used is not on your PATH the confirmation says to add it. The command is for macOS and Linux; on Windows the menu item says so.

In a terminal

clew open Projects/Grant\ proposal.md     # a note, in its vault
clew open ~/Notes/Research                # a vault
clew new --daily                          # today's diary entry
clew new "Inbox/Call with Sam"            # a new, empty note
clew export --pdf Projects/Grant\ proposal.md                     # beside the note
clew export --pdf Projects/Grant\ proposal.md --out ~/Desktop/    # elsewhere
clew open <file or folder>
A folder opens as a vault. A file opens in its vault: the nearest folder above it that holds .clew or .obsidian, else a vault Clew knows that contains it, else its own folder. Relative paths are read from where you are.
clew new --daily · clew new <note>
As the new link: today's entry, or an empty note at that path inside the vault, never over a file. Add --vault <name or path> to say which vault; without it, the vault in front, or the last one you had open.
clew export --pdf|--latex|--html <note> [--out <file or folder>]
Exports the note as File → Export would — --pdf is PDF via LaTeX — and writes only the file asked for: Grant proposal.pdf, .tex or .html. A PDF is typeset in a temporary folder that is removed afterwards, so no LaTeX build files appear beside the note; its images and its bibliography are still found from the note's own folder. Without --out the file goes beside the note. --out puts it elsewhere: a file name, or a folder — one that exists, or written with a trailing / — relative to where you run the command, with ~ meaning your home folder. If the PDF fails, the command says so with LaTeX's first error, and nothing is left beside the note. The export follows the vault's trust exactly as the menu's does: in a restricted vault, no note code runs.

The command is your own, typed by you, so unlike a link it opens a vault without asking — though a vault new to this device still opens restricted. It talks to the running Clew over a socket in Clew's settings folder that only your user account can reach. When Clew is not running it starts it first, and what you asked for opens in the window Clew starts with. It prints what it did — opened Projects/Grant proposal.md in Research, created Inbox/Call with Sam.md in Research, exported …/Grant proposal.pdf — and exits with 0 when it did it, 1 when it could not (and says why, e.g. no such file or folder), and 2 for a command it does not understand — or an --out with nothing after it — after printing its usage.

Reference

LinkDoes
clew://open?vault=V&note=P#Heading Opens note P of vault V at that heading, in a tab of its own
clew://open?vault=V&note=P&line=N The same, at line N
clew://open?vault=V Brings vault V forward
clew://new?vault=V&daily=1 Today's diary entry, created if missing; a notice says so
clew://new?vault=V&note=P A new, empty note at P (P 1 if taken); a notice says so
Anything elseRefused by name
CommandDoes
clew open <file or folder> Opens a vault, or a note in its vault
clew new --daily [--vault V] Today's diary entry, created if missing
clew new <note> [--vault V] A new, empty note, never over a file
clew export --pdf|--latex|--html <note> [--out F] Writes only that file — beside the note, or at F (a file, or a folder that exists or ends in /) — under the vault's trust
Exit status 0 done · 1 failed, with the reason · 2 usage
Installed by Help → Install the clew Command… → /usr/local/bin/clew, else ~/.local/bin/clew; macOS and Linux
